title: Comparison 3 · 3D reconstruction of β-gal (projection stack + Euler → volume)
summary: Project a β-gal map at 50 Euler angles, then back-project the stack with recon.bp to recover the volume. The canonical reconstruction self-consistency demo.

steps.title: Try 3D reconstruction
steps.body:
The endpoint of cryo-EM is recovering a 3D structure from many 2D particle images at random orientations. The workhorse operation is **back-projection (BP)** — smear each 2D projection back along its known viewing direction into 3D and sum. Ideally the original volume reappears. `recon.bp` also exposes the equivalent Fourier version (central-slice insertion) via `method=bp3g/bp3n`.

In this tutorial:
  1. Load the **β-galactosidase** test volume (shipped RELION 3.0 tutorial map).
  2. Use **data.sim.projections** to make 50 projections at known Euler angles (ground-truth angles kept).
  3. Feed stack + eulers_csv into **recon.bp** to recover the 3D volume.

Unlike real data, here angles are known exactly and there's no noise — perfect for observing what BP recovers in principle.

steps.title: Drop the β-gal node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · β-gal**. β-galactosidase is a standard test specimen in cryo-EM; the bundled map comes from the RELION tutorial reconstruction.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.betagal` shows its default image before we switch it to volume mode.

steps.title: Click β-gal
steps.body: Click the β-gal node. The Inspector shows `variant` (which of image / stack / volume to emit), `class_index`, and `size`.

steps.title: Set variant to map3d
steps.body: Change `variant` to **`map3d`**. The right-hand output port flips to `volume` (variant automatically switches the active port). β-gal's 3D density map is now available.

steps.title: Set size to 64
steps.body: Change `size` to **64**. 64³ voxels keeps the tutorial runtime in seconds (native is 128³). For real analyses use 128 or higher.

steps.title: Drop Sim · Random Projections
steps.body: From Data, drag **Sim · Random Projections** (`data.sim.projections`). This handy node projects an input volume at **n random Euler angles** and emits the stack plus a per-frame `eulers_csv`. With the ground-truth angles known, we can verify that BP recovers the structure as expected.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.sim.projections` produces an initial baseline output before we wire the volume in.

steps.title: Wire β-gal.volume → Sim · Projections.volume
steps.body: Drag from β-gal's `volume` output to Sim · Projections' `volume` input so the β-gal map is the source volume to project.

steps.title: Click Sim · Projections
steps.body: Click Sim · Projections. The Inspector shows `n` (number of projections), `seed` (RNG seed for angle generation), `uniform_sphere` (whether to spread uniformly on S²), `shift_sigma` / `noise_sigma` (optional artifact injection).

steps.title: Set n to 50
steps.body: Change `n` to **50** — 50 uniformly distributed Euler-angle projections. More → finer reconstruction; fewer → striation artifacts from angular undersampling.

steps.title: Drop recon.bp (3D back-project)
steps.body: From Reconstruction, drag **3D back-project / Fourier insert** (`recon.bp`) — the 3D reconstruction node. The `method` dropdown in the Inspector switches between four algorithms (bp3f / bp3d / bp3g / bp3n).

steps.title: Wire Sim · Projections.stack → recon.bp.stack
steps.body: Drag from Sim · Projections' `stack` output to recon.bp's `stack` input — the 50 2D projections flow into BP.

steps.title: Wire Sim · Projections.eulers_csv → recon.bp.eulers_csv
steps.body:
Drag from Sim · Projections' `eulers_csv` output (string port) to the ◇ marker on recon.bp's **`eulers_csv`** parameter (the wireable mark on the left). The ground-truth Euler angle for each frame is passed to BP.

This is the key: BP cannot put a projection back into the volume unless it knows which viewing direction the projection came from. With real data, angles come from an alignment step; here we hand the ground truth directly, so reconstruction should be clean.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body:
Press ▶ Run graph. β-gal map → 50 projections → BP → recovered volume. The recon.bp node shows a 3D volume.

Flip through central slices and compare with the original β-gal map. With 50 uniform Euler angles + exact angles + no noise, BP returns a volume close to the original. Success looks like: the central-slice barrel structure and the C2 (really D2) symmetry of β-gal survive back-projection.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
**Play with it:**
  - Swap `recon.bp`'s `method` between bp3f (default, ramp-filtered) and bp3d (no ramp correction) — the low-frequency bias BP picks up without ramp filtering becomes obvious (= the ramp filter visualised). bp3g / bp3n (Fourier insertion) show a different striation pattern from real-space BP.
  - Drop Sim · Projections' `n` to 20 — undersampling-induced striation becomes visible.
  - Raise `n` to 200 — details come back.
  - Set `noise_sigma = 0.5` — see how BP degrades under realistic noise.
  - Set `symmetry` to c2 — a cyclic-symmetry constraint effectively doubles the projection count (β-gal is actually D2; c2 already helps).

Real-world flow goes the other way: noisy particles → alignment estimates angles → BP. Here we exercised the clean 'angles known → project → recover with BP' pipeline to internalise the principle. For angle estimation, try the `angle_assignment` challenge.
